doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Sinatra, Shirley Horn and film songs
title: Mulligan's concert jazz band charts of I Want to Live! themes
summary: Mandel wrote three charts of his I Want to Live! themes for Gerry Mulligan's concert jazz band, which Stan Getz later recorded.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Three of those tunes, “Barbara’s Theme,” and, “Black Nightgown,” and the theme from, I Want to Live! you did charts for Gerry Mulligan on.
That Mulligan recorded with a concert jazz band.
Yeah, I think so, right, yeah.
So he basically, he just called you and said I like all these tunes that I played on the score or heard on the score and I’d like you to do charts for my band?
Yeah, it was it, and I was around New York at that time, so I went and rehearsed the band and all that stuff.
Apparently he brought Holman east to work in New York…
That’s right; Bill was with us at the same time.
So you just did those three charts then? You didn’t do anything else?
Yeah, that’s all ‘cause I’d left New York after that, went back home to California.
But he recorded all three of them.
Great, well with those players, good God, you could’ve written stuff that wasn't very good and it would've sounded terrific.
Yeah, Stan Getz later recorded, “Barbara's Theme.”
That’s another thing I didn’t know, you have to watch Stan Getz at all times or he’s libel to record something of yours.
